sonnet.problem: Stop 1 card 18 already asked, and showed the answer to, the fact that the leaders swore an oath to the Gibeonites. This card asks the same fact again, as the reason Israel doesn't attack.
sonnet.rule: An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact. Two lines that make the same point get one question. An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.

sonnet.problem: Stop 2 card 8 already asked that the Gibeonites will cut wood and carry water for the whole congregation, and card 11 retold it. This card asks it again. It also packs two claims into one statement: serving the congregation, and serving the altar.
sonnet.rule: It never re-asks the same fact. ... A true or false statement tests one claim.

sonnet.problem: The question says Joshua acts "with no word from the LORD." Verse 14 says only that the men of Israel "did not seek the counsel of the LORD." Not seeking counsel is not the same as the LORD saying nothing, so the card stretches the text.
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open. ... Don't stretch the text.

sonnet.problem: Moses first appears in the passage's text here (v24), and the earlier mention in stop 1 card 1 ("after Moses") doesn't say who he is. No card gives a short label like "Moses, Israel's leader."
sonnet.rule: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."
